resources.string: Part of Performance Mode

Everything here except the RAM slider and the MobileGlues options applies only while Performance Mode is ON. Leave a setting on Auto (or at its default) and the game runs exactly as Performance Mode always did. A flag you type in the Java arguments always wins over these settings. Changes apply the next time the game starts, and the game log lists the ones that are in effect.
Memory

Network and logs
Anti Crash
Reset
From %1$d MB up to %2$d MB on this phone (%3$d MB of RAM in total). The top of the slider stays below the total because Android closes the game when it needs more memory than the phone has free.
Reset Advanced settings
Puts the 24 performance settings and the three Anti Crash switches back to their defaults. The RAM slider and the MobileGlues options are not touched.
Put every Advanced setting back to its default?
Advanced settings were reset
Starting heap
How much heap the JVM sets up at launch; the most it can grow to is the RAM slider. A bigger start avoids pauses while the heap grows. Memory is only used as the game fills it.
Class memory trigger (Metaspace)
How much class data the JVM collects before its first cleanup. A modded game loads tens of thousands of classes, and a higher trigger means fewer cleanups while it loads. It does not reserve memory.
Compiled-code space

Room for the code the JIT compiles. When it is full the JVM stops compiling for good and the game slows down, a known cause of a sudden FPS collapse with many mods (look for \"CodeCache is full\" in the game log). It is reserved address space, not used RAM.
Pre-touch the starting heap
Touches the starting heap while the game loads, so memory page faults do not happen while you play. Starting takes longer and that memory is used at once.
Deduplicate strings (G1 only)
Lets G1 merge identical strings in the background. Saves some memory for a little CPU.
Garbage collector
G1 is the default. Parallel and Serial run no background threads; try them if the game log shows long pauses. A collector typed in the Java arguments always wins.
Pause goal
The longest pause the collector aims for (G1 and Parallel). A lower goal means shorter but more frequent collections.
Young generation size (G1)
How much of the heap holds new objects. A larger one clears short-lived garbage in small quick collections; a smaller one leaves more room for long-lived data.
G1 region size
An array that fills half a region or more is allocated in a slower special way. Larger regions turn fewer arrays into that.
Emergency headroom (G1)

Heap kept free so G1 can always copy objects. When it runs out (\"to-space exhausted\" in the game log) the collector falls back to a long full pause, which is a freeze. More headroom costs usable heap.
Garbage collector threads
How many threads share a collection. On a phone with two fast and six slow cores, fewer threads can keep a pause from waiting on a slow core. Auto lets the JVM decide from the core count.
Ignore System.gc() calls
Some mods ask for a full collection by hand, which freezes the game for a moment. On: those requests are ignored.
Process references in parallel
A modded game creates many weak and soft references; processing them on several threads shortens pauses.
JIT compiler

Auto uses the full two-tier JIT. The simple one (C1 only) compiles faster with less CPU, heat and native memory but reaches a lower top speed. It is also the usual fix for a crash inside Java\'s optimising compiler; Anti Crash can switch to it by itself.
JIT compiler threads
Threads that compile code in the background. Fewer leave more CPU for the game while it warms up, but code gets compiled later.
CPU cores the game sees

The JVM sizes its collector and compiler threads from this number, and Minecraft sizes its background worker pool as cores minus one. Fewer cores means fewer threads competing with the render thread, but chunks may load more slowly.
Lower helper-thread priority
Lets the launcher lower the priority of the game\'s background helper threads while the render thread is kept waiting or the phone is hot. Off: every thread keeps the priority Android gave it.
Screen refresh rate

Highest asks the screen for its fastest mode, up to 120 Hz. Pick a lower rate if the game cannot hold it: a steady 60 looks smoother than a rate that keeps dropping. Android may still decide otherwise.
Keep the refresh rate
Android sometimes lowers the refresh rate on its own. On: the launcher asks for the chosen rate again, waiting longer each time and not at all while the phone is hot.
Heat watch

Reads the phone\'s temperature (warm from 40 °C, hot from 42.5 °C) and raises the render thread\'s priority. The refresh-rate watch and the helper-thread scheduler also use it to back off when the phone is hot. Off: none of that happens.
Tell Android the game is playing

Android 13 and newer: tells the system when the game is loading and when you are playing, so a phone with Game Mode can give it the right resources. Whether anything changes depends on the phone maker. It does nothing on older Android.
Prefer IPv4 for servers
Skips IPv6 when connecting to servers. Helps when joining a server is slow or times out on mobile data. It does not change FPS.
GC pause lines in the game log
Adds a line to the game log for every garbage collection, so a stutter can be matched to a pause.
Performance report in the game log
Every 30 seconds writes memory, CPU and heat figures to the game log. The cost is tiny; off saves it.
Skip Java flags this Java does not know
Without this, one flag that the installed Java version does not know stops the game before it starts. On: unknown flags are ignored instead.
Lower RAM after a low-memory close

If Android closed the game because the phone ran out of memory, the next start uses an eighth less RAM, up to three times and never below 512 MB. Changing the RAM slider, or turning this off and on, undoes it. Needs Android 11 or newer.
Right now: %1$d step(s) taken off the RAM setting.
Simple JIT after a compiler crash
If the last crash happened inside Java\'s optimising compiler, the next starts use the simple compiler (C1 only). Turning this off and on undoes it. Needs Android 11 or newer.
Right now: the simple compiler is in use because of a compiler crash.
